keys.statement: Integrate the surplus heat of the exothermic ethylene oxidation with the energy-hungry glycol dehydration and separation section; in this plant the retrofit targets cut external heating by about 93% and cooling by about 45%.

plain.title: Ethylene glycol plant: use the ethylene oxide reactor's surplus heat in the glycol section
plain.when: One section exports heat (the exothermic ethylene oxidation) while another imports it (glycol dehydration and separation).
plain.do: Heat-integrate the reaction section with the glycol section.
plain.why: Matching a heat source with a heat sink replaces external utilities on both sides.
plain.check: Run a pinch analysis (heat-recovery targeting) on the whole plant, columns included, to get the targets.
plain.result: In Ali et al. 2022's plant the retrofit targets cut external heating by about 93% and cooling by about 45%.

decisions.obstacle: One section exports heat while another imports it.

keys.statement: Include reboilers and condensers in the pinch analysis, and place each column so it sits entirely above or entirely below the pinch.

plain.title: Include reboilers and condensers in the pinch analysis, and keep each column on one side of the pinch
plain.when: You run a pinch analysis (heat-recovery targeting) on a plant with columns.
plain.do: Include every reboiler and condenser in the stream data. Place each column entirely above or entirely below the pinch (the temperature where heat recovery is tightest).
plain.why: A column that straddles the pinch moves heat across it.
plain.check: Plot each column's reboiler and condenser temperatures against the pinch temperature.

source.locator: Pinch analysis of the full system, p. 15

decisions.obstacle: Columns left out of heat integration.
decisions.mechanism: A column across the pinch moves heat across it.
decisions.operation: Analyse the full system; place columns on one side.

keys.statement: Never transfer heat across the pinch, which costs twice in utilities; at the pinch, match streams so the hot stream's heat-capacity flow is no larger than the cold one's above the pinch and no smaller below it.

plain.title: Never move heat across the pinch
plain.when: You design the heat exchanger network after a pinch analysis.
plain.do: Never transfer heat across the pinch. At the pinch, match streams so the hot stream's heat-capacity flow (mass flow times heat capacity) is no larger than the cold stream's above the pinch and no smaller below it.
plain.why: Heat moved across the pinch must be supplied again as hot utility and removed again as cold utility, so it costs twice.
plain.check: Compare the network's utility use with the pinch targets; any excess points to a match across the pinch.

decisions.mechanism: Cross-pinch transfer raises both hot and cold utility.

keys.statement: Place heat engines such as steam turbines to reject heat below the pinch; in this plant that reduced external cooling by about another 6%.

plain.title: Steam turbine or other heat engine: let it reject its heat below the pinch
plain.when: You integrate a heat engine such as a steam turbine into the plant's heat network.
plain.do: Position it with the grand composite curve (net heat flow against temperature) so that it rejects heat below the pinch.
plain.why: Heat rejected below the pinch replaces heat that would otherwise go to cooling.
plain.check: Check on the grand composite curve that the engine's exhaust temperature lies below the pinch.
plain.result: About another 6% less external cooling in Ali et al. 2022's plant.

decisions.mechanism: Rejecting heat below the pinch uses heat that would otherwise go to cooling.
decisions.operation: Position the engine using the grand composite curve.
